summary.text: 太 is a marked form of 大, used for meanings such as ‘great’, ‘very’ and ‘excessive’. The distinguishing dot separates the graph from 大; the evidence does not establish that the dot depicts an object or represents a sound. [ref003, ref014, ref005]

formation.text: Indicative: a differentiating form of 大 made by adding a dot as a distinguishing mark. The evidence supports this graphic function, but does not establish a semantic or phonetic function for the dot. The supplied accounts calling 太 pictographic or phono-semantic, and the mnemonic of a person for scale, are not supported by the paleographic evidence here. [ref010, ref014, ref001, ref003]

components.text: 大 is the base graph. The added 丶 is a distinguishing mark; its original meaning and any sound value are not established here. The graph is analyzed as formed by adding this mark to 大. [ref010, ref014]
丶 is the visible dot added to distinguish this graph from 大. No independent object, meaning or sound function for it is established by the evidence. [ref014, ref017]

history.text: The curated comparison image is a modern seal-script-style rendering of 大, not an ancient 太 form; the evidence reports early distinguishable 太 shapes in Western Han inscriptions, including 太初, while proposed earlier forms are disputed or read otherwise. This does not establish a complete sequence of graphic forms. [ref014, ref022]

Pre-Qin texts used 大 for words later written 太; the graph 太 appears as a distinct form in the Western Han account. This graphic differentiation should be kept separate from the history of the spoken words. [ref010, ref015]

uncertainties.text: The available evidence does not establish a unique semantic path from ‘big’ to ‘very’ or ‘too’, nor does it show that the dot depicts a person or supplies a sound. The specialist account cautions that individual occurrences of 大 need contextual interpretation. [ref010, ref011, ref014, ref017]

Reported Western Han dates and readings come through the paleographic article; no dated primary artifact image was independently inspected here. The identity of some alleged pre-Han 太 forms remains disputed. [ref014]

senses.text: The character is associated with ‘great’ and ‘big’; evidence for its earlier use must be read in context, since pre-Qin texts often used 大 for words later written 太. [ref003, ref005, ref010, ref015]

太 is used as a degree word meaning ‘very’ or ‘much’. Excavated-text interpretations report degree-adverb uses written with 大, and sometimes 泰, before 太 became a distinct graph; these readings do not establish a single linear semantic development. [ref002, ref005, ref016]

The sense ‘too’ or ‘excessive’ is reported in the etymological account and in interpretations of early degree-word uses written 大. The evidence does not securely order this sense against ‘very’ or ‘great’. [ref003, ref005, ref016]

limitations.text: The evidence supports overlapping associations with ‘great’, ‘very’ and ‘excessive’, but does not establish a dated chain connecting them or a priority among these senses. The reported earliest distinguishable graph is Western Han; it does not by itself date the word’s earliest use. [ref010, ref011, ref014, ref016]

overview.text: 太 marks 大 with a dot to distinguish the graph. It commonly means ‘very’ or ‘too’, with associations to ‘great’; the dot is supported as a graphic marker, not as a picture or sound cue. [ref014, ref005, ref017]

components.text: 大 supplies the base graph associated with ‘great’ or ‘big’. [ref003, ref010]
The dot distinguishes 太 from 大; its own meaning is not established. [ref014, ref017]

relationships.text: 大 is the base graph in the proposed differentiating formation of 太 and is associated with ‘big’ or ‘great’. [ref003, ref010, ref014]
丶 is the added distinguishing mark in the paleographic analysis; the evidence does not assign it a semantic or phonetic value. [ref014, ref017]
